## Zhang Liang · Liu county is enough
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhang-liang/asking-for-less/
Source: Records of the Grand Historian, Hereditary House of the Marquis of Liu
Tags: Deep read, Zhang Liang, Asking for the small thing at the summit

You are told to name your own reward. Do you take the largest one available? Here is why he took the smallest.

### Q: What actually happened?
With the empire settled, Liu Bang told him to choose thirty thousand households anywhere in Qi, the highest grant then possible. He declined. He had raised troops at Xiapi and met His Majesty at Liu, and that meeting was heaven's doing: enfeoff me at Liu and it is enough; I dare not accept thirty thousand households. Liu was a small county. He then pleaded illness, took up the regimen and gave up grain, saying he wished to drop the affairs of men. Of that founding generation Han Xin was killed and Peng Yue destroyed. Zhang Liang died in his bed.

### The parts · Asking for the small thing is a signal
Thirty thousand households is not money, it is a base with its own revenue and its own men. What he turned down was the structure, not the wealth. Choosing a small county announces in public that he does not intend to grow into a problem somebody will eventually have to solve.
e.g. Winning the big account and then splitting it across two teams reads as generosity this quarter. It is really you declining to become the thing that has to be broken up.

### The parts · Give the other side a version it can repeat
He did not say he was afraid of being suspected. He said Liu was where they met and that heaven had arranged it. The true reason spoken aloud would have shamed them both. Offering a version everyone can live with is not insincerity, it is leaving people room to move.
e.g. To get off a project, I think this will fail starts an argument. I am worth more on the other thing ends the same way and keeps the relationship intact.

### The parts · Leave while people still want you to stay
He began withdrawing at the point of maximum credit and maximum usefulness. The timing and the proceeds of an exit run in opposite directions: the later you leave, the less there is to collect and the worse it looks going out the door.
e.g. Hand over while the numbers are good and the persuasion to stay is sincere. The identical handover after two bad quarters is a different event with a different name.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: something has gone well and a large reward is available for the asking.
Ask first: once you hold it, do you become a problem that someone above you has to manage? Say the answer out loud before you decide.
Where it goes wrong: converting every bit of credit into position; or, on the way out, stating the real reason so plainly that neither side can stay in the room.

### Lines to keep
Enfeoff me at Liu. That is enough. I dare not take thirty thousand.
I wish to drop the affairs of men and follow Master Red Pine.
He declined not the money but a structure somebody would later dismantle.

========================================================================
## Zhang Yiming · Delayed gratification
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhang-yiming/delayed-gratification/
Source: Interview with Caijing, 2016, and his early microblog posts
Tags: Deep read, Zhang Yiming, The trait he rates highest

Asked which quality he values, he keeps giving one answer. What the phrase actually means in his hands.

### Q: What actually happened?
In interviews Zhang Yiming has said that delayed gratification is one of the qualities I value most, and that graduates who put never losing out first are spending themselves in advance. In his usage the phrase covers three layers. Choosing work: do not trade the fastest-growing seat for this year's salary. Building product: hold off monetising, as early Toutiao pushed commercialisation back and worked the recommendation engine and retention first. For the company: refuse to be satisfied by the result of the current fight. His own gloss on the reverse side is that most people want too badly to win the round in front of them.

### The parts · What is delayed is the payout, not the feedback
The common misuse is to invoke it while enduring years with no signal at all. In his practice the feedback is immediate, data watched daily, retention chased daily, and only the conversion into money and reputation is postponed. Delay with feedback is investment; delay without it is self-admiration.
e.g. Holding revenue back while growing, with the retention curve checked every day. Without that curve it is not delayed gratification, it is drifting.

### The parts · Cashing in early has a hidden price: compounding stops
The cost of early monetising never shows on the statement. Damage the experience for this period's revenue and you shrink the base that every later period grows from. The trait is really a compound-interest sum: move the payout later so the principal turns more times. People who can do the arithmetic need no willpower.
e.g. One more ad slot on the home screen lifts this month and is deducted from retention three months out. Put both curves on one chart and restraint stops being a virtue.

### The parts · It is a filter for choosing people, not only a private discipline
He applies the trait in hiring, by looking at a candidate's past choices: always the highest current pay, or sometimes the steepest slope? Every move on a curriculum vitae is a delayed-gratification question already answered, and it answers more honestly than an interview does.
e.g. Two records: one where each move added thirty per cent of salary and no capability, one with two pay cuts to change field and real command now.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: a payout now and a steeper growth slope are sitting side by side.
Ask first: during the delay, do I have a signal I can observe, and what does the compound arithmetic say the gap is?
Where it goes wrong: using delayed gratification to grind through a dead end with no feedback; or delaying for ever and leaving the fruit to rot on the tree.

### Lines to keep
Delayed gratification is one of the qualities I value most.
Most people want too badly to win the round in front of them.
Graduates who put never losing out first are spending themselves in advance.

========================================================================
## Zhang Yiming · An ordinary mind for extraordinary things
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhang-yiming/ordinary-mind/
Source: ByteDance ninth-anniversary all-hands speech, March 2021
Tags: Deep read, Zhang Yiming, The ninth-anniversary speech

A company known for ferocity spent its ninth anniversary on composure. The specific kinds of interference he named.

### Q: What actually happened?
At ByteDance's ninth anniversary in 2021 Zhang Yiming's all-hands had a single theme: keep an ordinary mind while doing extraordinary things. He named the common distortions. Toward the past, vanity about achievements or self-pity about setbacks. Toward competition, watching the rival so closely that the rival leads you. Toward the future, targets set so far from reality that anxiety eats the effort. His argument is that lifting attention off the patterns and the noise and seeing the present as it is produces better judgement. Extraordinary results come from an ordinary state of mind held at the decisive moments.

### The parts · Watching the rival hands over the steering wheel
Excess attention to competition means the agenda gets taken over: they ship and you answer, they attack and you defend. It looks like fighting back, but you are already executing their strategy for them. Composure here is concrete. A rival's move is one input, and its weight should not exceed your own user data.
e.g. A team that calls an emergency alignment for every competitor launch finds a year later that the roadmap was written by the other side. Make it a monthly review.

### The parts · Vanity and self-pity are the same coin
Pairing them is exact. Pride in past success and grief over a setback run on the same mechanism, with attention locked on me rather than on the thing. Decisions made in either state serve a self-image: one proving it still has it, the other proving it was unfair.
e.g. After a winning streak you cannot kill a project you started; after a loss you rush a comeback. Opposite moves, one driver.

### The parts · Targets within reach keep anxiety from taking over
A target detached from reality does not produce drive, it produces anxiety, and anxiety distorts judgement systematically: short horizons inflated, fundamentals skipped, remedies grabbed at random. Composure is not the absence of ambition. It is ambition cut to a scale you can reach on tiptoe.
e.g. Break number one in three years into two verifiable milestones this quarter. Same ambition: one phrasing manufactures anxiety, the other manufactures progress.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: competition is white-hot and the team swings between elation and dread.
Ask first: how much of this week's agenda was set by the other side, and are we looking at the thing or at ourselves?
Where it goes wrong: reading composure as refusing to fight the fights that have to be fought; or saying ordinary mind while the targets and the review cycle are still designed by anxiety.

### Lines to keep
Keep an ordinary mind while doing extraordinary things.
Watch your rival too closely and you end up being led.
See the present as it is and judgement improves.

========================================================================
## Zhu Yuanzhang · Be slow to take the title
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhu-yuanzhang/delay-the-title/
Source: History of Ming, Life of Zhu Sheng; Veritable Records of Ming Taizu
Tags: Deep read, Zhu Yuanzhang, Do without the name for now

Everyone who rose at the same time was claiming a throne. He was the one who did not, and it was worth eleven years.

### Q: What actually happened?
In 1357, having taken Huizhou, he went to see the old scholar Zhu Sheng and asked how to settle the empire. Zhu Sheng gave him nine characters: build the walls high, store the grain widely, be slow to take the title. Around him, Han Lin'er was the Little Prince of Brightness, Xu Shouhui had declared himself emperor, Zhang Shicheng was the Prince of Cheng, Chen Youliang would call himself emperor of Han. Everyone with strength was grabbing a name. He followed the nine characters for eleven years, while the Yuan armies spent them on the men who had claimed first.

### The parts · A title is an act of switching your own light on
The name brings a power to summon people, and it also gives your coordinates. The moment the title is hung on you, you stop being a roving band and become a regime that has to be destroyed first. Before you can absorb concentrated fire, a name is a liability.
e.g. Announcing that you intend to lead the industry before the model works gets you onto every incumbent's watch list at once. Two quiet years cost far less.

### The parts · The three go together, or not at all
High walls are the ability to defend, wide stores the ability to last, slow titles the ability to stay unlit. The third alone is just hiding; the first two alone are a large obvious target. Because you are accumulating and can hold, you have earned the right to wait.
e.g. Working quietly without building any defence means the thing is copied by the time you surface. A low profile only pays while you are also walling and storing.

### The parts · When to claim it is a separate judgement
Slow does not mean never. He waited until Chen Youliang and Zhang Shicheng had both been destroyed, the Yuan court was fighting itself, and the whole south was his. The test was not whether he felt ready; it was whether anything outside still had the strength to concentrate on him.
e.g. The moment to announce a change of direction is not set by how prepared you are inside, but by whether anyone outside still has capacity to come at you.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: you have some results and you are wondering whether to announce them loudly.
Ask first: once I announce, who moves me to the top of their list, and can I take that?
Where it goes wrong: staying quiet without building any wall, which wastes the wait; reading slow to take the title as never showing your face.

### Lines to keep
Build the walls high, store the grain widely, be slow to take the title.
The day the title goes up, your coordinates go up with it.
Slow does not mean never. Wait until nothing outside can concentrate.

========================================================================
## Zhu Yuanzhang · Heavy punishment for officials
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhu-yuanzhang/heavy-law/
Source: History of Ming, Treatise on Punishments; The Grand Pronouncements
Tags: Deep read, Zhu Yuanzhang, A broken age needs a heavy hand

He put officials to death by the tens of thousands. This is about how he himself defined the range this method applied to.

### Q: What actually happened?
He was merciless about corruption: an official who took sixty taels was executed, and each prefectural and county yamen had a skinning ground beside it, the stuffed skin set next to the seat of office. He compiled the Grand Pronouncements, printed the actual cases, distributed them across the empire, required every household to keep a copy and put them in the examinations. When the heir said the punishments were too heavy, the History of Ming records his answer: I govern a broken age, so the punishments cannot but be heavy. You will govern a settled one, and yours can be light.

### The parts · Heavy punishment is for resetting expectations
By the end of the Yuan, administration had collapsed and officials generally assumed that graft had no consequences. To break that assumption the penalty has to be heavy enough that everyone recalculates. It is a one-off cost of resetting, not a way to run things — he said so himself.
e.g. In a team where nobody has been held to account for years, the first case has to be handled heavily and in the open, or the assumption that nothing happens survives.

### The parts · Cases travel further than clauses
The Grand Pronouncements printed real cases rather than abstract statutes: who, where, what they did, what happened to them. An abstract rule makes each reader work out whether it applies to him; a case hands him the comparison directly, and costs far less to spread.
e.g. Nobody finishes the compliance policy. Write up last month's real breach and how it was handled in three hundred words, and by evening everyone knows where the line is.

### The parts · He set an expiry date and nobody honoured it
Inside I govern a broken age there is a self-limit: the method has conditions, and when they go it should go. The trouble is that severity, once institutionalised, will not leave on its own — it grows an enforcement apparatus that depends on it. Later Ming harshness is what stayed.
e.g. Emergency approval powers created during a crisis are almost never withdrawn afterwards, because the department holding them has built its reason to exist around them.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: a class of problem keeps recurring and you are considering heavier penalties.
Ask first: is this one reset of expectations, or how I intend to run things from now on? If the first, when does it end?
Where it goes wrong: publishing clauses instead of real cases; turning a crisis measure into a standing institution with no way out.

### Lines to keep
I govern a broken age, so the punishments cannot but be heavy.
You will govern a settled age, and your punishments can be light.
Severity that has been institutionalised will not leave on its own.

========================================================================
## Zhuangzi · The use of being useless
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhuangzi/use-of-uselessness/
Source: Zhuangzi, In the World of Men; The Mountain Tree
Tags: Deep read, Zhuangzi, What nobody requisitions lives longest

Making yourself useful is instinct. What being useful costs you at the same time.

### Q: What actually happened?
A master carpenter passes an oak so vast it could shade thousands of oxen, and doesn't look twice. Asked why, he says: it's useless timber — boats from it sink, coffins rot, tools break. Good for nothing, and so it has lived this long. That night the tree comes to him in a dream: the fruit trees get torn apart the moment the fruit ripens; their ability is what harms them. I have sought uselessness a long time, and only now have it. Then Zhuangzi turns it on people: everyone knows the use of the useful; nobody knows the use of the useless.

### The parts · Useful is a qualification to be requisitioned
Once a person is judged unusually good at something, that something arrives without end. It looks like being valued. It is being fixed in one position and spent there — the ability itself becomes the source of the load.
e.g. Whoever is best at firefighting gets all the fires. Three years on, they're the least replaceable and the least improved person on the team.

### The parts · Useless is the room you keep for yourself
The useless tree survived by not appearing on anyone's list. People need a portion of time and ability that isn't counted as output — it produces nothing immediately, and it is the only part nobody else gets to schedule.
e.g. Put half a day a week in the calendar and hold it. Everyone will call it a luxury, and it decides whether you can do anything else a year from now.

### The parts · Don't exhaust yourself in a single position
Zhuangzi isn't against being useful. He's against being useful as the only way of existing. Used to the limit means completely defined, and the moment that use isn't wanted the person expires with it.
e.g. A team that only knows one line of business fails entirely when the cycle ends. Not for lack of effort. They were too competent.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: you're the one on the team who can carry anything, and you're busier every month.
Ask first: the thing I'm best at — what position is it fixing me in?
Where it goes wrong: treating being needed as safety; converting all of your hours into output you can report.

### Lines to keep
Good for nothing, and so it has lived this long.
Everyone knows the use of the useful. Nobody knows the use of the useless.
The cinnamon is edible, so it is cut down.

## Zhuangzi · The cook and the ox
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhuangzi/ox-carving/
Source: Zhuangzi, The Secret of Caring for Life
Tags: Deep read, Zhuangzi, Go along the gaps

One cook replaces his blade monthly, another hasn't in nineteen years. Where exactly the difference sits.

### Q: What actually happened?
Cook Ding carves an ox for Lord Wenhui and the movement looks like dancing. Asked how his technique got so good, he says what he cares about isn't technique. At first he saw a whole ox; after three years he no longer saw a whole ox; now he meets it with the spirit rather than looking with the eye. A good cook changes his blade yearly, because he cuts. An ordinary one monthly, because he hacks. His has done thousands of oxen in nineteen years and the edge is as if newly whetted — because he has been travelling in the gaps between the joints.

### The parts · The blade stays sharp because it never meets the hard part
The edge has no thickness and the joints have space; something thin entering something wide moves easily. Struggle isn't a shortage of force. It's the wrong place to put the blade. Every hard collision is a positioning problem.
e.g. A push that meets resistance everywhere usually means the entry point sits where the interests are densest. Enter where nobody objects and it moves itself.

### The parts · See the structure before you talk about technique
Ding's three stages — seeing a whole ox, ceasing to see a whole ox, meeting it with the spirit — are increasingly fine readings of structure. Technique is a by-product of that reading. Train it in the other order and you are training force.
e.g. A new hire handles a complaint with scripts. A veteran hears which step it's actually stuck at. The difference is the map in their head.

### The parts · Slow down where it knots
Ding isn't smooth throughout: at every knot he sees the difficulty, grows wary, slows, and makes his movements smaller. Real fluency isn't speed the whole way. It's knowing where you must go slowly.
e.g. For the two steps most likely to go wrong, add a check instead of adding speed. People with one tempo have all their accidents in one place.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: something is hard to push at every point, and you're considering pushing harder.
Ask first: is my blade in a gap or on a bone?
Where it goes wrong: substituting force for position; holding one tempo throughout and not slowing where you most need to.

### Lines to keep
The joints have space, the blade has no thickness.
At every knot I see the difficulty, grow wary, and slow down.
I meet it with the spirit and do not look with the eye.

========================================================================
## Zhuangzi · Things being equal
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhuangzi/equalizing-things/
Source: Zhuangzi, Discussion on Making All Things Equal
Tags: Deep read, Zhuangzi, Whose ruler is this

Two people argue to the end and neither is convinced. Why Zhuangzi says a third person won't settle it either.

### Q: What actually happened?
Zhuangzi asks an almost mischievous question. A person sleeping somewhere damp gets a bad back — does a loach? A person up a tree is frightened — is a monkey? Of the three, who knows the proper place to live? He extends the logic to argument: if you beat me in a debate, are you actually right? Bring a third person to judge, and whether they agree with you or with me they have already taken a side. How could they settle it? This isn't abolishing right and wrong. It's a reminder that right and wrong always speak from inside some standard.

### The parts · Before arguing, ask whose ruler is being used
There is a right and wrong on that side too, and one on this side. Most deadlocks aren't disputes about facts, they're disputes about standards — each conclusion holds inside its own. Until the standards are on the table, no amount of discussion converges.
e.g. Engineering says the design is good because it's maintainable; the business says it's bad because it ships late. Both are right. They're scoring different functions.

### The parts · The third party brings a standard too
Calling in a more senior person looks neutral and is really introducing a third standard. It ends the argument by authority rather than by understanding, so the same disagreement reappears unchanged the next time.
e.g. The boss rules and both teams comply. Three months later the identical fight happens on a different project.

### The parts · Move position and the ruler changes
Zhuangzi's method isn't finding the one correct ruler. It's acknowledging where your own came from. Do that and the other conclusion stops being 'wrong' and becomes 'true under his conditions' — and then you can discuss conditions instead of correctness.
e.g. Swap 'your plan won't work' for 'given we're prioritising the ship date, what does your plan cost?' Same subject, different conversation.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: a disagreement keeps recurring and never resolves.
Ask first: what is each side optimising? Can both targets hold at once?
Where it goes wrong: ending it by authority without touching the difference in standards; treating the other conclusion as an error rather than as correct under other conditions.

### Lines to keep
There is a right and wrong on that side, and one on this side.
If you beat me in the argument, are you actually right?
Of the three, who knows the proper place to live?

========================================================================
## Zhuge Liang · The plan at Longzhong
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhuge-liang/longzhong-plan/
Source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Shu, Biography of Zhuge Liang
Tags: Deep read, Zhuge Liang, The first half is what not to touch

A twenty-seven-year-old lays out a strategy that governs the next several decades. Its hardest work is done in the opening section.

### Q: What actually happened?
Asked for a plan after the third visit, he began not with what to attack but with what could not be. Cao Cao has a million men and holds the emperor: you cannot contend with him. Sun Quan has held the east for three generations, the ground is hard and the people attached: he can be an ally, not a target. Two of the three biggest pieces on the board are crossed off before anything is chosen. Only then the available ones, Jing and Yi, and the conditions: hold both, keep the alliance, put the government in order, and when there is a change, move by two roads.

### The parts · The first half of a strategy is elimination
Rule out what cannot be beaten and what should not be touched, and what remains is the actual menu. Most strategy discussions skip the step and open with what we should do, which spreads the money across several fights that were never worth entering.
e.g. Before the annual goals, write the list of what we are not doing this year and get agreement on it. That list moves the budget more than the goals do.

### The parts · Different relations for different stronger parties
Both are out of reach, and he treats them differently: one cannot be contended with, the other can be an ally but not a target. Filing everyone stronger than you under enemy is how a plan ends up isolated. Naming which one must be joined is what makes it stand.
e.g. Of the two giants in your industry, one has to be avoided head-on and the other may supply you or send you traffic. Treat both as rivals and the road narrows.

### The parts · Write the trigger condition down
When there is a change in the empire is the whole plan's trigger. He never claims a date. He says that until the condition appears, everything being done is preparation. Writing the trigger down stops both mistakes: firing early, and not being ready when it fires.
e.g. When the rival's main product visibly stalls, we commit. Write that sentence down, and name the number that counts as stalling, or it becomes a mood on the day.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: you are setting the next direction and there are more options than resources.
Ask first: which of these can you plainly not win, and which of those should be joined rather than fought? Write both lists before the third one.
Where it goes wrong: listing only what you will do; or keeping the trigger condition in your head instead of writing it as something anyone can check.

### Lines to keep
You cannot contend with him.
He can be made an ally. He cannot be taken.
When there is a change in the empire, move by two roads at once.

========================================================================
## Zhuge Liang · Near the worthy, far from the small
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhuge-liang/close-the-worthy/
Source: The Memorial on Sending Out the Army
Tags: Deep read, Zhuge Liang, It is about who can reach you alone

Eight characters usually read as a moral instruction. What he means is narrower and more mechanical: who is able to see you privately.

### Q: What actually happened?
The memorial states it as cause and effect. Keeping near to worthy officials and far from small men is why the Former Han rose; the reverse is why the Later Han fell. Then, instead of moral advice, he arranges channels. Palace and government office are one body; reward and punishment must not differ between them. On matters in the palace, consult Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi and Dong Yun. On matters in the camp, consult Xiang Chong. And a warning: do not belittle yourself, and so block the road along which honest advice arrives.

### The parts · Near and far describe a channel, not a preference
A small man is not effective because he flatters well. He is effective because he holds a route to the decision maker that nobody else has. Cut the route and the same person has no influence at all. The thing to manage is the structure, not the character.
e.g. Someone goes around every review straight to the boss and it works once. After that everyone copies him. The fix is not the man, it is the route he used.

### The parts · Belittling yourself blocks the road too
Do not belittle yourself and so block the road of honest advice is the half nobody quotes. A leader who keeps saying he does not understand and is not much good leaves people unable to judge what is worth reporting, so they report less. Excessive modesty and deafness produce the same silence.
e.g. I do not really follow the technical side, you decide sounds open for a month. After six, a serious risk goes unreported because nobody knows if saying it does anything.

### The parts · Name the people and the subjects
He does not say listen to good advisers. He pairs names with subject matter, one line at a time: for this class of question, that man. Named to a person, the channel is real. Left as a principle, the channel is decorative.
e.g. Important decisions should involve more voices means nothing. Naming the three roles that must be heard, with none of them skippable, changes the structure.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: you suspect that what reaches you has been reshaped on the way.
Ask first: how many routes exist that reach you without passing through anyone, and who is currently using each of them?
Where it goes wrong: blaming the character of one person; or replacing a named channel with a principle about listening to more people.

### Lines to keep
Near the worthy and far from the small men: that is why they rose.
Do not belittle yourself and block the road honest advice comes along.
Palace and office are one body. Reward and punishment must not differ.

========================================================================
## Zhuge Liang · The tears, and then the demotion
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zhuge-liang/executing-ma-su/
Source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Shu: the biographies of Zhuge Liang and Wang Ping
Tags: Deep read, Zhuge Liang, He put himself on the same list

Executing the man he had promoted is not the hard part of this story. What he did immediately afterwards is.

### Q: What actually happened?
On the first northern campaign he passed over Wei Yan and Wu Yi, whom everyone had recommended, and gave the vanguard to Ma Su. At Jieting Ma Su went against the deployment, left the water and camped on the hill; Zhang He cut the water off and destroyed him. Back in Hanzhong, Zhuge Liang executed him to answer to the army. Then he sent up a memorial asking to be demoted three ranks, with the charge spelt out: I was not clear-sighted about men, and muddled in handling affairs. He went from chancellor to general of the right.

### The parts · Punish only the executor and the fault leaks downward
The error happened in execution, but the choosing and the authorising happened above it. Handling the executor alone announces that the deciding layer carries no consequences, so the same failure returns by the same route, because the cause was never touched.
e.g. The project fails, the project manager is disciplined, and the person who approved it is untouched. The next project comes apart at the identical seam.

### The parts · Self-demotion has to name the charge
He did not say responsibility rests with me too. He wrote the specific count: not clear-sighted about men. That is a charge somebody can hold up against his later behaviour. Vague self-criticism binds nobody. A named one gets remembered and used.
e.g. We all share the blame says nothing. I approved the schedule without checking it gives people a sentence to quote back at you next time.

### The parts · Weep, and carry out the law
He was as close to Ma Su as to a son and executed him anyway; then mourned him personally and raised his children. Feeling and rule each ran their own course at full strength. Using the feeling to suspend the rule, or the rule to prove you have no feeling, is half a job either.
e.g. Letting go a long-serving colleague you like: the severance, the thanks and the introductions are all real, and the decision does not move.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: a failure needs accounting for, and the person who got it wrong was the one executing.
Ask first: who chose him and who authorised it, and what happened to that person? If the answer is nothing, the case is still open.
Where it goes wrong: closing the file once the executor is dealt with; or stopping your own account at the contentless phrase that you share the blame.

### Lines to keep
He executed Ma Su to answer to the army.
I was not clear-sighted about men, and muddled in handling affairs.
By the rule of the Spring and Autumn, the commander answers for it.

========================================================================
## The Comprehensive Mirror · Talent and character
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zizhi-tongjian/talent-and-virtue/
Source: The Comprehensive Mirror, Zhou chronicles, book one
Tags: Deep read, The Comprehensive Mirror, The dangerous man is the able one

The first argument in the first book of the whole work is about choosing people. This is about why it sits there.

### Q: What actually happened?
The book opens with the partition of Jin, and its first great event is the fall of Zhibo. Zhibo had five qualities above other men — bearing, horsemanship, skill, eloquence, decision — and one lack: he was not humane. On this Sima Guang hangs the first of his own comments. Talent is the resource of character; character is the commander of talent. He sorts people into four: both complete is a sage, both absent is a fool, character over talent is a gentleman, talent over character is a small man. Then blunt advice: failing a sage or a gentleman, take the fool.

### The parts · Talent is an amplifier; character sets the direction
Character commands, talent supplies — the image means talent has no direction of its own. The same ability doubles the return in a right direction and doubles the loss in a wrong one. So the stronger the person, the larger the damage when the direction is wrong. That is arithmetic, not moralising.
e.g. An outstanding engineer who disagrees with the architecture accrues technical debt faster than three ordinary ones, because he writes more and writes it faster.

### The parts · A fool's damage has a ceiling
His reasoning is utilitarian. A fool who wants to do harm lacks the means and is easy to guard against; a capable man of bad character does harm nobody can stop. Where you cannot judge conduct, choosing the lower ceiling of ability is a way of capping the worst case.
e.g. In a critical seat, a middling person with clear boundaries beats a brilliant one who keeps crossing them. The first has a low ceiling and a high floor.

### The parts · The trouble is that we see talent first
He names the root: talent is easy to see and character is not. An interview can measure ability and cannot measure where someone stops; a record can list the wins and not how they were obtained. The bias is therefore systematic, not occasional.
e.g. Every selection process leans towards demonstrable ability. To balance it you have to design a stage that examines conduct, and not hope one appears.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: a candidate is clearly the strongest and something about how they operate worries you.
Ask first: if they turn that ability in a direction I do not want, can I stop them?
Where it goes wrong: reading it as a sermon about virtue; testing only ability at interview and never designing a stage that tests where someone stops.

### Lines to keep
Talent is the resource of character; character is the commander of talent.
Character over talent is a gentleman, talent over character a small man.
Rather than get a small man, get a fool.

========================================================================
## The Comprehensive Mirror · Worth copying, worth avoiding
URL: https://ourword.ai/en/i/zizhi-tongjian/what-to-keep/
Source: Sima Guang, memorial on presenting the Comprehensive Mirror
Tags: Deep read, The Comprehensive Mirror, Fix the selection rule first

One thousand three hundred and sixty-two years of events. This is about the single rule that decided what went in.

### Q: What actually happened?
He ran the compilation for nineteen years and the finished work runs to two hundred and ninety-four volumes. In the memorial presenting it he set out how he chose: cut what was long-winded, gather what was essential, take only what bears on the rise and fall of the state, on whether the people prospered or suffered, what is good enough to copy and bad enough to warn. Shenzong, naming it, called it a mirror of what has been, useful to the art of governing. One rule throughout, which is why there is almost no ornament and almost nothing kept for completeness.

### The parts · Set the rule first or you never finish
Nineteen years, thirteen centuries of material: without a selection rule you can apply mechanically, the work is infinite. Take only is the condition that let the book be completed. He did not know what to write; he knew clearly what not to.
e.g. A survey with no stated exclusion rule never ends, because any new material looks worth one more look. Write down what you will not read and progress starts existing.

### The parts · The rule has to admit the bad
Bad enough to warn stands beside good enough to copy. A library of successes only teaches that there is one road that works. Failures usually carry more information, because a success can be accidental in many ways and a failure's mechanism is generally clearer.
e.g. A company that records best practice and never records post-mortems teaches new people a method assembled entirely from survivors.

### The parts · The rule has to be executable by someone else
The work was divided between Liu Ban, Liu Shu and Fan Zuyu, with Sima Guang over the whole. A taste that exists only in the editor's head cannot be divided. Only a rule written down and applied identically by three people will hold for nineteen years.
e.g. If the content standard lives only with the editor, quality collapses the moment the team grows. Write it as three rules another person can apply.

### Q: How do I use it today?
Where you are: there is too much material and you are hesitating over what to include.
Ask first: what is my selection rule, and can I write it as one sentence someone else could apply?
Where it goes wrong: keeping only the successes; leaving the rule in your own head, where it cannot be divided up.

### Lines to keep
Cut what is long-winded; gather what is essential.
Good enough to copy, bad enough to warn.
A mirror of what has been, useful to the art of governing.
